items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: I mean he didn’t have an Irving Mills like Ellington had or Cab Calloway, somebody like that.

ctx.x: He wasn’t that effective a leader.

No. He wasn’t. Not at all. No. He just wasn’t. They talk about that accident that happened, the car accident, which after that he seemed very aloof and not really interested much in promoting the band very much. But even before that I kind of wonder how much of a leader he really was. I mean he didn’t have an Irving Mills like Ellington had or Cab Calloway, somebody like that. I mean Hammond sort of came in at some point and sort of tried to take the band, do stuff with the band and stuff, and get them recording…

Well a question — I don’t know if I would have had it back then — but I’ve never really been clear about Benny Goodman’s role with this integration thing and how that happened. And you had said something to me yesterday about it. And Helen Dance had talked about her role in that. But what’s your take on exactly how it happened.
